clue.text: Sugar, perhaps, needing part, say, for complete payment

parts.note: a lump of sugar is a cube; 'perhaps' marks sugar as one example of something sold in lumps

indicators.note: 'say' tells you the word for 'part' is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: some means a part or portion of something

explanation.surface: Someone sweetening a deal: sugar is offered as a portion towards settling a whole bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A single payment made all at once, covering the full amount rather than instalments, is the standard sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Possibly toxic sanction well short

parts.note: to let is to permit or sanction

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: hale means well, in good health

explanation.surface: A warning that a contaminated well might be poisonous unless sanctioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something potentially deadly could well be poisonous, which is the sense of possibly toxic.

clue.text: Solver left a bit

parts.note: Inspector Morse, Colin Dexter's Oxford detective

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver departed a little while ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece or mouthful, a little bit of something.

clue.text: Tell tales about duke on starter of tempura being least fat

indicators.note: the two words go about the duke, enclosing him

parts.note: to spin a yarn is to tell it
lies are false tales

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of the word tempura

explanation.surface: Gossip about a duke dining on tempura, who is still the thinnest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell tales' reads as one phrase meaning gossip, but it splits into two separate words; 'about' then puts the duke between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindly means long and thin, so the superlative is the skinniest, the one with least fat.

clue.text: Solver, member of secret society

definitions.meaning: a Freemason, of the fraternal order known for its secrecy

explanation.definitionFit: Perry Mason solves cases, and a Freemason belongs to a famously secretive brotherhood.

clue.text: Gold, auric edges in pen containing a metalloid

indicators.note: 'in pen' says the gold and the edges go inside the word for a pen

parts.note: a Bic is a well-known make of ballpoint pen
OR is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: 'edges' asks for only the first and last letters of the word auric

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab description: gold, golden-edged, in a pen holding some semi-metal element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is a brand-name ballpoint, not a writing instrument in general or an enclosure; 'edges' keeps only the ends of 'auric'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boracic acid is derived from boron, an element classed as a metalloid, so the adjective describes something holding boron.

clue.text: Like a rabbit, say, albeit modified in corporeal form

indicators.note: 'modified in corporeal form' puts the rearranged letters inside the body word

parts.note: bod is informal for body

indicators.note: modified means the letters of albeit are altered in order

explanation.surface: A rabbit, albeit one changed into a physical body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'albeit' looks like a mere conjunction but is the fodder that 'modified' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits have short stubby tails, so they are an example of animals with a docked or short tail.

clue.text: Piffle on a list

parts.note: piffle and rot both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: Nonsense written on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster of duties or names in turn is a kind of list.

clue.text: Solver a shade upset about Paul, ultimately, as writer

parts.note: Charlie Chan, Earl Derr Biggers's fictional detective

indicators.note: the colour word goes about the final letter of Paul, enclosing it
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: red is a shade, a colour

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of Paul

explanation.surface: A detective turning red-faced over the setter Paul, who is credited as an author.
explanation.walkthrough: RED reversed is DER; the L from Paul goes inside to give DLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote the Philip Marlowe detective novels such as The Big Sleep.

clue.text: Best solver embodying Holmes, initially

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within a body, so the solver encloses the letter

parts.note: Albert Campion, Margery Allingham's gentleman detective

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Holmes

explanation.surface: The finest detective is one who personifies Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holmes' suggests a detective, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: As an informal British adjective it means excellent or first-rate, as in 'a champion idea', the same as top-quality.

clue.text: Groups of bones in this ratio passed to the left

indicators.note: passed to the left says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mathematical instruction to shift a ratio leftwards, oddly said to involve bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to ISRAT sitting inside 'this ratio'; read right to left it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsus is the cluster of small bones in the ankle; the plural names several such clusters.

clue.text: Lower seams burst as tight on both sides of tanga

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, so the letters of 'burst as' stagger into a new order
'both sides of' takes just the first and last letters of tanga

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction: seams split because the fabric was stretched tight on either side of a tanga bikini bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'tight' (drunk) is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology, underlying layers or seams of rock are the deeper strata beneath the surface.

clue.text: Scot, a head welcoming lecturer in religious education

indicators.note: a head welcoming something takes it inside, so the head word is split open

parts.note: bean is informal for a person's head

indicators.note: 'lecturer in religious education' puts the lecturer inside the school subject

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is the old British school subject of religious education
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A Scottish school head greets a lecturer who teaches religious studies.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, is the older British name for the school subject now called RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Aberdeen, a city in north-east Scotland, is by definition a Scot.

clue.text: Relish decline

definitions.meaning: a savoury sauce into which food is dunked
to sink or fall, as prices or a road may

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a creamy sauce for crisps and a downward slope or fall.

clue.text: Eliciting a yawn perhaps as beginning to nod, rip undies off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are spoiled and reordered
beginning takes the first letter of nod

explanation.surface: A dull, sleepy scene of someone nodding off as underwear is ripped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'rip off' but signals the anagram of N plus RIP UNDIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and lacking imagination bores its audience, and boredom makes people yawn.

clue.text: David was his second outstanding challenge, I suspect

indicators.note: read as 'out-standing', the short word stands outside the rest

parts.note: mo is a short moment, as in 'wait a mo'

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone says that a famous David sculpture was the artist's second great challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise; split as out-standing, it puts MO around the shuffled 'challenge I'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance sculptor carved the celebrated marble statue of David in Florence, so it was his work.

clue.text: Last of money on account invested in reminder to put on his evacuated bloomers

indicators.note: money invested in something is placed inside it, so these letters go inside the reminder word

parts.note: a hint is a prompt or reminder

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of money
evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of his

explanation.surface: Financial jargon about money in an account mixed with a reminder to put on bloomers, the underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests underwear, but it is flowers that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyacinths are spring flowers, things that bloom, so bloomers is a playful name for them.

clue.text: It suggests I step on virgin snow

parts.note: read as wordplay, a rearranged form of the word piste, with off as the anagram signal, gives the clue's I step

explanation.surface: A skier's footprint on fresh untrodden powder.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, treated as an instruction, scrambles PISTE into I STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing away from the prepared runs means going onto untracked, untouched powder.

clue.text: In general, violin required for solver

indicators.note: 'In general' puts the violin inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: A sentence claiming that, generally, a violin is needed by a puzzle-solver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' looks like 'generally'; it means inside a general.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Lestrade is the Scotland Yard detective in the Sherlock Holmes stories.

clue.text: Deliver position that's autonomous

parts.note: to deliver someone is to set them free
one's standing is one's position or rank

explanation.surface: A sentence about delivering something to a spot that runs itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing on its own without support or attachment is independent, hence self-governing in a loose sense.

clue.text: Ending in ignorance, solver finds god in the dark

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of ignorance

parts.note: Inspector John Rebus, Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective

explanation.surface: A detective, after a spell of ignorance, discovers a deity while groping in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the primordial deity who personifies darkness.

clue.text: Conclusion of narrative in unfolding story, a world of possibilities?

indicators.note: 'in unfolding story' puts the letter inside the rearranged word
unfolding means opening out, so the letters of story are spread into a new order
conclusion means the final letter of narrative

explanation.surface: The end of a tale arrives in a developing story full of potential.
explanation.definitionFit: From the saying 'the world is your oyster', meaning every opportunity is open to you; the question mark flags the idiom.

clue.text: Weed in pool

definitions.meaning: the total stake in a game of poker, the kitty

explanation.definitionFit: The same short word is slang for cannabis and the gathered stakes in a card game.

clue.text: Wood given pen to outline role of someone directly involved

parts.note: fir is a kind of tree and its timber

indicators.note: to outline something is to draw round it, so the pen word surrounds the role

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Carpentry and writing mixed: wood and a pen used to sketch a role for someone directly concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and contracts a first-party matter belongs to one of the principals themselves rather than an outsider.

clue.text: Solver as pack member

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.definitionFit: Sam Spade solves cases, and a card of one suit belongs to a deck.

clue.text: Copy walls in southern part of church

indicators.note: walls means encloses, as walls surround a space

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: A replica built with walls inside the southern section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church is a familiar architectural feature.

clue.text: Downtrodden thing in the way, a solver

indicators.note: 'thing in the way' puts the trodden-on item inside the word for a road

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a carpet is literally trodden down underfoot

explanation.surface: Someone tripping over a doormat-like person who stands in their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downtrodden' suggests a victim, but it is literal: something walked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Kay Scarpetta is Patricia Cornwell's forensic investigator, a fictional crime solver like the other detectives in this puzzle.

clue.text: Capital given stick by artist

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist
a bat is a stick used to hit a ball

explanation.surface: A capital city handed a walking stick by a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Unseeing as a 25-letter alphabet, did you say?

indicators.note: 'did you say' asks for the description to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: an alphabet of 25 letters has no I in it, which can be put as I-less

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking whether a blind person is like an alphabet missing a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the letter I from 26 and you get 25: 'I-less', which is heard the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no eyes means being unable to see, so the word describes blindness.

clue.text: Eventual consumer always touring state in Midwest America

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the word for always goes round the rest

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
ND is the abbreviation for North Dakota, a Midwestern US state
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A shopper forever travelling around a Midwestern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The final purchaser who actually uses a product is the last person in the supply chain.
